x: Stan Vickers was the sole Belgravian walker in the Kent County Championship at Hayes and came home with the individual title with a time of 83.49, over a rather long ten miles. Further south, in Hampshire, Norman Guilmant took 2nd place in the Championship of that County.

A trio of Hugh McGreechan, Bob Newson and Norman Guilmant were at this time some three minutes behind with George Beecham, Harry Shields and Cyril Yescombe completing the team a further 2 minutes back.
Of our second four, McGreechan showed that he is on the way back to his old form and Norman Guilmant gave clear indication that the longer distance events will find him a worthy contender.
George Beecham who took it steady at the start, walked well to finish 6th and Bob Newson over the last four miles, passed Norman Guilmant and really got moving to finish 8th.

Behind these two an interesting battle was going on for third place between Bob Newson, Hugh McGreechan and Norman Guilmant. The last named tried hard to steal a lead but Bob and Hugh would not let him get away.

George Beecham finished 13th with Norman Guilmant 17th and Harry Shields 32nd. Our President tried hard to catch the Woodford man in front of him over the last couple of miles but failed by 20 seconds.

A team sponsored by the Union of London Walking Clubs visited Belgium on July 15th to compete in an International race over 50 k.metres and included in the team were two of our walkers, Norman Guilmant and George Checkley.

George Checkley however, who seems to relish such conditions, had moved into an early lead in front of our second man Bob Newson, with Norman Guilmant also moving strongly and it looked rosy at halfway.

When Redhill was reached it was then Norman Guilmant's turn to strike a bad patch and he was obliged to stop for a few minutes. After this however things began to change for the better with George recovering and Norman getting away again.
Ray Hall gained revenge on Ray Switzer, Norman Guilmant smiled his way through and was last seen selling old football jerseys to the timekeepers.
We started a full team of eight, with Ray Switzer and Norman Guilmant as individuals. Our hopes rested on Eric Hall, second last year at Enfield where it rained throughout.
Following his illustrious predecessors Tommy Green and Norman Guilmant Pat Duncan became the third Belgravian to win this race and the first man to beat eight hours for the trip.

Belgrave have their share of heroes Tommy Green four times winner, Norman Guilmant won it, L.C.Allen and Harry Shields won the veteran's award, Ray Hall one of six men who have bettered the magical eight hour barrier and George Beecham holder of more winning team medals than any other man.

Belgrave hopes rose for the first Belgrave man to win this race since 1954 when Norman Guilmant took the title. Moullin was now moving very well and although our 3rd and 4th men were surrounded by hostile forces their experience could be relied upon in the later stages.

The following year Norman Guilmant took Belgrave's first individual medal since 1937 when he finished 2nd. In 1954 the Club rounded off a triumphant season by taking both individual and team honours in the 'Brighton'.

The walkers had their triumphs, none more so than Norman Guilmant over the longer distances who after his second place in the Brighton won international colours in Italy where he, unfortunately, collapsed but no lasting harm was done.
